results.title: Johatsu
results.overview: Meysam and Parisa discover that a mistake has been made during the burial of a family member in a village; an incident that soon draws everyone into the matter.

results.title: Psalms of Sorrow
results.overview: Worn down by a failing body and a father who has fallen into silence, Isaac is forced to choose between saving himself and remaining true to his conscience in a world where survival comes at a heavy price.

results.title: Paradise
results.overview: Paradise follows a trans gardener whose deep connection to the natural world becomes a guide for understanding who they are. Shot on 16mm, together with original hand-painted animation, this poetic hybrid documentary is a kaleidoscopic celebration of the deep interconnections between ecology, queerness, and creativity. Paradise weaves the personal with the environmental, offering a tender portrait of growth, resilience, and rebirth.

results.title: Spainter
results.overview: In the midst of war, a color pencil found on the battlefield awakens a sniper’s forgotten childhood passion for painting, forcing him to confront the violence that erased it.

results.title: A Real Grey Area
results.overview: Attempting to stage an historical reenactment on Coney Island, a contractor working for a powerful client speaks with a representative from a rental company regarding the unconventional use of an electric generator.

results.title: Polyphem
results.overview: Polyphem is the second chapter in a series of short experimental landscape films that reinterpret the stages of the journey of Homer‘s Odyssey and set them in the context of the anthropocene. Filmed in the only active bauxite tailings pond in Germany, Polyphem reimagines the myth of Polyphemus from Homer’s Odyssey within a contemporary landscape scarred by red mud, industrial aluminium waste.

results.title: Can GPT Dream of a Pink Elephant?
results.original_title: Can GPT Dream of a Pink Elephant?
results.overview: The film stages quasi-clinical encounters between aphantasic individuals and an AI system, then re-films digital footage on 8mm to return synthetic vision to material fragility.  Approximately 4% of the population has aphantasia, an inability to form visual images in the mind’s eye. They understand what an elephant is, what pink is, yet see nothing when they close their eyes. The film places this absence of inner images in dialogue with an AI system that produces images excessively, asking whether synthetic vision and human non-vision might reveal each other.

results.title: Roman Charity
results.overview: Building on my background in academic drawing, I create a painting that reinterprets Rubens’ Roman Charity from the viewpoint of its female figure. This painting then appears as a prop in the video, becoming a means to inscribe my own biography and to explore questions of gaze, female subjectivity, memory, and the boundaries of the permissible.

results.title: Textus Connectivus
results.overview: The household plastic tarpaulin so widely used in cities becomes a source of distortions in space and time, as if the laws of quantum mechanics had been transferred to the macroscopic world. Places far apart are gathered into a single field that lives by its own paradoxical rules. We find ourselves inside a cinematic arabesque, in which shots join into a continuous, intricate ornament unfolding in time.

results.title: RAW
results.overview: RAW. A visual-sonic ritual.  A manifesto of vulnerability.  Raw material whose hidden interior is looking for a way to be spoken.The film is an inquiry into bodily memory and the impossibility of resonance.  Breathe in — as if lifting layers of earth.  If your throat is clenched — let the body talk.  Breathe out — let a feeling take on flesh.  You are here. You sound. You breathe.

results.title: Me Too (Make Films)
results.overview: A novice documentarian wants a place at film school and sets out to shoot a study of an interesting person. Finding no one at 11 at night, she ends up at the Smolensk Cemetery, at Aleksei Balabanov’s grave. Trying to make a film of it, she comes away with a string of botched sketches: a couple on a first date; a painter who has spent years on a portrait of Balabanov;people who turn up to drink and argue about cinema. It was dark, the camera pointed the wrong way, she had promised not to show a thing, she walked out on her subject. Everything that mattered was not caught on camera, and so it was drawn.

results.title: Mother
results.overview: A single day was enough to split Svetlana’s life into “before” and “after.” Her husband left, leaving her to face a new reality on her own. For a year and a half, the camera was in the hands of her eldest daughter. This candid documentary chronicle tells the story of how a woman and her loved ones learn to live a new life, grappling with their fears and discovering new strength.

results.title: The Logger
results.overview: “It’s warm at home” — a thought that carries the lumberjack as he cuts firewood in the winter taiga. He sees himself back with his wife and four children: first the stove, warmth for his own household, then the rounds selling wood to other houses, putting a little money by for the family. He is afraid that before long he will have to leave them.  The taiga itself seems to help him. But the taiga is a force beyond human command: it can warm, and it can burn, taking what is dear.

results.title: Women’s Circle
results.overview: Two closest friends, Elina and Ramilya, on the cusp of turning 40, take a recreational trip to the mountains. Elina brings along her new lover, Vasily, hoping the trip will strengthen their relationship. Away from it all, she sees that Vasily is making advances towards Ramilya that her friend does not reject. Jealousy takes over Elina, and the holiday she had waited for turns into a psychological duel. Can their friendship survive the test?

results.title: If I’m Not a Realist
results.overview: Sergei, an artist from Siberia in a creative and personal crisis, hides in his studio from his debts, his family, and himself. Then his daughter turns up with a camera — the one person who wants to reach out to him, and the one person he is willing to let in. As they draw unexpectedly close, they start looking for a way forward.

results.title: It’s Time to Come Home
results.overview: Inside a military hospital we watch the lives and fortunes of people learning to adapt to a new reality. Following a long and hard rehabilitation process, the New Year is coming, with all its festive bustle, and after that, the long-awaited discharge.

results.title: Hair Curlers on a Bald Man
results.overview: The exploratory film “Hair Curlers on a Bald Man” is dedicated to Georgy Frantsevich Millyar (born de Milieu), a unique figure in Soviet cinema — the actor who played “every imp, troll, and hobgoblin”, the unforgettable Baba Yaga and the allegorical Koschei in the fairy-tale films by Alexander Rou, as well as a host of other parts and walk-ons. Drawn from documents in the Russian State Archive of Literature and Art, the Museum of Cinema, Mosfilm, the Gorky Film Studio, Gosfilmofond, the Russian State Archive of Film and Photo Documents, and the Gelendzhik Museum of Local History, the film turns into Millyar’s own archive — a mythical territory where the actor’s life and the history of Soviet cinema assemble into a collage on memory and on a person’s place in history.

results.title: Big Phan
results.overview: For nearly 50 years, two unseen masters of their craft—Dave Raymond and Tom Burgoyne— have brought to life the Phillie Phanatic, a character they had to become if they were ever going to become themselves.

results.title: Sins of an Amish Husband
results.overview: Sarah is a devout Amish woman who suspects foul play after her sister, Ida, dies in a mysterious barn fire. Driven to protect her young nephew, Sarah begins investigating her brother-in-law.
